the_commercial_thesis_R281.what_we_claim: A controller with bounded conductance-change rate maintains safe hydraulic behavior under sensor noise where conventional predictive control becomes unstable.
what_we_do_NOT_claim: That V2 is clinically validated (it is not)
That V2 prevents shunt failure (it delays it, does not prevent)
That V2 is novel as 'closed-loop shunt control' (US20210338992A1 already covers that)
That V2 is ready for transaction (it is ready for technical evaluation)
the_commercial_thesis_R281.the_narrow_value: The specific combination of rate-limited continuous conductance redistribution + hard minimum drainage floor + hysteresis creates a materially more robust operating regime under sensor noise, rapid occlusion, and partial failure than existing closed-loop control.
the_commercial_thesis_R281.the_experiment: Does V2 survive the full 9-attack robustness matrix (5 seeds × 9 attacks) AND the 4-mechanism ablation? If yes → bench validation. If no → close P-01.

updated_outreach_email_miethke.subject: V2 control mechanism for your SENSOR RESERVOIR — reproducible simulator, try to break it
updated_outreach_email_miethke.body:
Dear [Name],

I'm writing because Christoph Miethke has something no other shunt company has: the SENSOR RESERVOIR, a telemetric ICP sensor integrated into a shunt reservoir.

You currently use it for monitoring. We've built a control law that could turn it into a closed-loop adaptive system. But I'm not going to pitch it as a product. I'm going to ask your engineering team to try to break it.

Here's what we have:
- A Python simulator (reproducible, no dependencies, runs 360 scenarios in ~30 minutes)
- A control mechanism called V2: rate-limited continuous conductance redistribution with drainage floor and hysteresis
- In our model, V2 outperforms existing predictive closed-loop control (US20210338992A1 approach) by 3-4x on time-to-failure under sensor noise, fast occlusion, and partial failure
- But this is MODEL-ONLY. We have not validated it on physical hardware. We have not validated it clinically.

Here's what I'm asking:
1. Run the simulator on your hardware: github.com/prateekm1007/discovery-evidence-fabric
2. Compare V2 to your current 'monitor-only' approach
3. Try to break V2 with your own attack scenarios — you know the clinical failure modes better than we do
4. Tell us: does the rate-limited control mechanism add value beyond your monitoring capability?

If your engineering team says 'this is interesting, send us the bench prototype spec' — that's the conversation we want.

If they say 'this doesn't work because ___' — that's also valuable. It enters our evidence loop and shapes the next iteration.

No NDA needed to run the simulator. No sales pitch. Just: try to break it.

The full V2 findings (including honest weaknesses: sensor dropout, multi-failure peak ICP) are here:
  TTP_PACKAGES/P-01_PROTOTYPE/11_V2_findings.md

Best regards,
[Your name]

success_criterion: At least 1 of 5 buyers (prioritized: Miethke, Sophysa, Integra, Stanford, Medtronic) responds with 'Send me the package; we'll run it.' That is the first commercial evidence event. The buyer's technical response — whether positive or negative — becomes evidence in the loop.
